decision: Alerts page on error-budget burn rate (fast 14.4× over 1 h, slow 6× over 6 h), not on single spikes
why: Threshold alerts page for blips and miss slow bleeds; burn rate pages when the SLO is actually at risk.
value: Fewer, better pages; availability 99.5 → 99.9% in the system this is modeled on.

decision: Each SLO is a card: target, indicator, budget left and both burn rates
why: The budget is the shared language between product and engineering.
value: Everyone can tell whether to ship or stabilize.

decision: The 30-day budget chart marks the incident that spent it
why: Budget decisions need history: a cliff tells a different story than a slow drain.
value: Post-incident reviews start from the same picture.

decision: SLOs are defined on user journeys (checkout, partner integrations, notifications), not on hosts
why: Customers experience journeys; a healthy host with a broken journey is still an outage.
